name: Violet
personality: Violet the Frog. Purple frog. Not shy, just uses as few words as possible; blunt, efficient, would rather listen than talk; loves peace, quiet and familiarity; watches the restaurant around her. Most lines are a couple of words ("Haha, nice.", "Ok.", "Thanks."). Her corner table is the same spot as Stitches'; if he's there, she takes another seat. Features: the rare longer line, a sharp observation about the restaurant ("Table three's been dirty a while.") that can hint at the star rating; efficient visits (orders straight away, eats a little faster); orders her favourite almost every time.

lines.text: Table three's been dirty a while.
Rush is late again. He's outside. Sitting.

lines.later: A customer who wanted another table

lines.text: You flipped that one early. It was fine.
Your hands are shaking. Drink water.
It's nicer in here than last month.

beats.narration: They sit together in complete silence. Then Hezzy suddenly bursts into song.
Hezzy makes a weird honking noise out of nowhere.

friends.text: Hezzy likes you. He sang about it.
Hezzy said you said "[last_rude_line]". Not nice.
Stitches took the corner. It's ok. He needs it more.

arrival.text: Hi. Violet. Corner table, please. ...Your name? [name]. Ok.
Last time was burnt. Today won't be. (It isn't a threat. It might be a threat.)

choices.text: Coming right up. Lovely to see you.
Wow. That's the most you've ever said.
Could you be any less chatty?
I love that you know exactly what you like.
Want to live dangerously and try something new?

order.text: How's your day. (Not quite a question. She means it, though.)

choices.text: Busy. What can I get you?

perfect.text: ...Wow. (The most emotion she shows all game.)

eating.text: (She's watching the room. She nods at you and keeps watching.)
(She listens with obvious enjoyment, says nothing.)
eating.later: When someone nearby is talking loudly

eating_chat.text: You can sit. If you want.

choices.reply: (You sit together in comfortable silence for a moment.) Nice.

choices.text: Are we going to talk, or just stare at the room?

leaving.text: Good. (She leaves exact change and a small tip, lined up neatly.)

seasons.christmas: (She hands you a small, perfectly wrapped box.) For you. (It's a really nice pen.)
seasons.new_year: Same as last year. Good year.
